newsitem.title: FRANCE: Saudi Arabia now seen buying barley in May - trade.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia now seen buying barley in May - trade.

text.p: Saudi Arabia may delay its return to world feed barley markets until May because it still has some stocks available, European grain exporters said.
Saudi Arabia may also buy less barley than the 800,000 to 900,000 tonnes forecast by French grain office ONIC in early March, they said.
Exporters initially expected Saudi Arabia, the world's largest barley importer, to shop for barley in mid-April.
"Nothing will happen on Saudi Arabia right away. Apparently they have barley in their stocks," one exporter said, adding this may delay imports.
Another exporter said that with the spring the Saudis can feed their animal herds on grass, which further eases import pressure.

In March the European Union awarded licences to export 1.1 million tonnes of barley on world markets. Exporters suggested some of these licences may be destined to cover future business with Saudi Arabia.
In January Saudi Arabia bought 1.2 million tonnes of optional-origin barley for February and March delivery, with the bulk going to the European Union.
The International Grains Council expects Saudi Arabia to import 4.7 million tonnes of barley in 1996/97 against 3.1 million tonnes in the previous campaign.
